clue.text: Cheerful brew pub to have food

indicators.note: to brew is to stir up and concoct, so the next word's letters get mixed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then mixed
to have food is to eat

explanation.surface: A happy afternoon: a brewpub where you can also get a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brew pub' reads as one familiar thing, a pub making its own beer, but 'brew' is working on 'pub' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Upbeat is a synonym of cheerful, describing an optimistic, positive mood.

clue.text: Get through to write review about Spielberg blockbuster

parts.note: to pen is to write
E.T. is Steven Spielberg's 1982 hit film
to rate something is to review and grade it

explanation.surface: A critic struggles to get through writing a review of a Spielberg blockbuster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' here means 'on the subject of', so the film sits beside the review word rather than inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To penetrate is to pierce or force a way through something.

clue.text: Matricide put God in office

parts.note: with 'in office' at the end, put in office means elect
Ra is the Egyptian sun god
completes the phrase put in office

explanation.surface: A mother-killer installs a deity in power.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'put in office' is split around God, but the god goes after the verb rather than inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend Electra helped her brother kill their mother Clytemnestra, so she is a mother-killer.

clue.text: Talking head baked a piece of chicken

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, which is all that is kept

parts.note: the first letter of talking
baked is slang for stoned, or high

explanation.surface: A television pundit has cooked a chicken portion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Talking head' looks like a TV commentator, and 'baked' like cooking, but baked is drug slang here.
explanation.definitionFit: The thigh is the upper leg joint of a chicken, a standard cut sold and cooked.

clue.text: Belief in Edmonton athlete's comeback maintaining soldier? No

indicators.note: a comeback here is a coming back the other way, so the team member's name is read from its end
to maintain is to hold, so the turned word holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: the Edmonton Oilers are the city's NHL ice hockey team
GI is an American soldier
N is the abbreviation for no, as in a Y/N answer box

explanation.surface: A sportswriter asks whether faith drove a hockey player's comeback, and a soldier answers no.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark and 'No' read as a soldier being turned down; 'No' simply adds its abbreviation at the end, after the soldier has gone inside the turned-around Oiler.
explanation.definitionFit: Religion is a system of faith, so a belief in the sense of a creed one holds.

clue.text: Strangle characters gathering for broker
Body of water that is perceived internally doesn't drop off

indicators.note: internally says the following pieces sit within the body of water

parts.note: a lake is a body of water
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is
to perceive something is to see it

explanation.surface: A lake, seen from within, never quite stops.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie awake is to stay sleepless in bed, so one does not drop off to sleep.

clue.text: Mischievous entity swapping Russian government's $1,000 for a different $1,000

indicators.note: swapping one thing for another means exchanging one letter for a different one

parts.note: the Kremlin is the seat of Russian government
G, for grand, is another abbreviation for a thousand dollars, replacing K

explanation.surface: Something mischievous switches the Kremlin's money for other money.
explanation.walkthrough: K (kilo) and G (grand) are both slang for a thousand dollars, so one stands in for the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A gremlin is an imaginary imp blamed for mechanical faults, a mischievous creature.

clue.text: Vegetable held over in Hanoi, normally

indicators.note: turned over in a down clue means read upward, from the end back to the start
held means contained, so the word is inside the run of letters that follows

parts.note: the letters spanning the end of Hanoi and the start of normally

explanation.surface: Some vegetable kept back in Hanoi, as usual.
explanation.definitionFit: An onion is a bulb vegetable used throughout cooking.

clue.text: Like a bull in a china shop or in a sandwich shop, house pet with energy

definitions.text: Like a bull in a china shop

parts.note: taken as written
a deli sells sandwiches
a cat is a typical house pet
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A clumsy brute in a china shop, or a cat bounding through a sandwich shop, wrecks everything.
explanation.walkthrough: The two shops look parallel, but only the second is wordplay; 'with' just joins the last piece on.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone like a bull in a china shop is clumsy and tactless, which is what indelicate means.

clue.text: Make needed changes, when retracting what goes out twice a day

indicators.note: retracting means drawing back, so the word that follows is taken back from its end

parts.words: what goes out twice a day
parts.note: the tide goes out roughly twice a day

explanation.surface: An editor's advice: revise your story when you are taking back what you said.
explanation.definitionFit: To edit a text is to revise it, making the corrections and changes it needs.

clue.text: After short time, discomfort and pain for a runner

indicators.note: after says the discomfort word comes later, placed behind the abbreviation

parts.note: ST is the dictionary abbreviation for standard time, a short form of a time
an itch is a mild physical discomfort

explanation.surface: Shortly into a race, a jogger feels first an itch and then a sharp ache.
explanation.walkthrough: ST is the abbreviation for standard time, as in the EST and PST time zones.
explanation.definitionFit: A stitch is the sharp ache in the side that runners often get mid-race.

clue.text: Communicating with a 15 under the weather

parts.note: 15 across is auntie, and Auntie Em is Dorothy's aunt in The Wizard of Oz
under the weather means unwell

explanation.surface: Getting in touch with a relative who is feeling poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference asks for a particular aunt: Auntie Em, from The Wizard of Oz.
explanation.definitionFit: Emailing someone is a way of communicating with them by electronic message.

clue.text: Onetime campaign manager to staff a military installation

parts.note: to staff a post is to man it
taken as written
a fort is a military post

explanation.surface: A political operative is assigned to run a military base.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul Manafort chaired Donald Trump's 2016 presidential campaign before his conviction.
explanation.definitionFit: Manafort is a person who once ran a presidential campaign, so the definition is by example of a real holder of that job.

clue.text: 30-day tyrant, having eliminated doctor one bit at a time, is forced to answer a difficult question

definitions.text: forced to answer a difficult question

indicators.note: having eliminated means taken out, so letters are removed from the two pieces
one bit at a time says the removal is spread out, a single letter from each piece in turn

parts.note: a month has about thirty days
a despot is a tyrant
MD, Doctor of Medicine, is a doctor

explanation.surface: A short-lived dictator, rid of his physician, is grilled by reporters.
explanation.walkthrough: The M of the doctor comes off the first piece and the D off the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Being put on the spot is an idiom for being pressed to respond to an awkward question immediately.

clue.text: A loose relative

parts.note: taken as written
to loose something is to set it free, or untie it

explanation.surface: A relative of easy morals, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loose' looks like an adjective describing the relative; it is a verb meaning set free.
explanation.definitionFit: An auntie is an aunt, a parent's sister and so a family relative.

clue.text: Nine large bats, as a rule

indicators.note: bats means crazy, so the letters before it are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, then mixed

explanation.surface: Nine big bats, as is usual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bats' looks like flying mammals or cricket bats; it is the adjective meaning crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: In general and as a rule are idioms meaning usually, in most cases.

clue.text: Congress, for instance, is initially scrupulous and precise

indicators.note: initially points to the opening of the word right after it, so only its first letter is used

parts.note: the first letter of scrupulous
exact means precise

explanation.surface: A civics lesson praising the US Congress as careful and exact.
explanation.walkthrough: Congress here is not the legislature but its older sense of sexual union.
explanation.definitionFit: Sexual congress is an old formal term for intercourse, so congress is one example of a sex act.

clue.text: In a vessel, Cruz misbehaved

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in says the senator's name goes inside the drinking vessel

parts.note: a cup is a drinking vessel
Ted Cruz is a US senator from Texas

explanation.surface: Senator Cruz behaved badly aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship, but it is a drinking cup.
explanation.definitionFit: To act up is the idiom for behaving badly, misbehaving.

clue.text: Those people keeping symbol back to front as a way to understand 5A

indicators.note: keeping means holding on to, so the people word holds the other piece inside it
the back of the word is moved to its front, so its final letter jumps to the start

parts.note: they means those people
a logo is a symbol of a company

explanation.surface: Some people, holding up a symbol, try to make sense of a faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 5 across is religion. 'Back to front' does not reverse the symbol word; it moves its last letter to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Theology is the systematic study of religion, a scholarly route to understanding faith.

clue.text: New York supports clear vandalism? That's a crime

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece that supports another sits beneath it, so the state goes last
vandalism wrecks things, so the letters of the word before it are smashed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then mixed
NY abbreviates New York, which supports by sitting below in a down entry

explanation.surface: Is New York in favour of plain vandalism? That would be criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: Larceny is theft of personal property, a criminal offence.

clue.text: Diana the Magician embraces abomination

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold within, so the phrase before it holds the word inside its letters

parts.note: the run of letters across the three words

explanation.surface: A stage magician named Diana takes on something hateful.
explanation.definitionFit: Anathema is something intensely loathed, an object of detestation, just like an abomination.

clue.text: What there is in team, ultimately: tennis with excellent racket

parts.note: the saying goes there is no I in team

indicators.note: ultimately points to what comes last, so the final letters of the following words are used

parts.note: the final letter of tennis
the final letter of excellent

explanation.surface: Team spirit, a tennis match and a top-quality racket, all thrown together.
explanation.walkthrough: The sports saying 'there's no I in team' supplies the opening. 'Racket' looks like a tennis racket but means a din.
explanation.definitionFit: A racket is a loud din, so noise is a synonym.

clue.text: Progenitor's paint in correct English?

indicators.note: correct English swaps a slangy contraction for a standard one, so one part of the word is replaced

parts.note: read as P followed by the slang contraction ain't

explanation.surface: Is an ancestor's paint described in proper English?
explanation.walkthrough: Read paint as P + AIN'T; proper English replaces ain't with aren't, giving P + ARENT. The question mark admits that 'aren't' is a stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: A parent is a direct progenitor, an ancestor from whom offspring descend.

clue.text: Quietly call up pattern

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading from the bottom, so the word is turned around

parts.note: to dial someone is to call them on the phone

explanation.walkthrough: 'Call up' reads as one phrasal verb; the 'up' is the instruction to turn the call word over.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaid is a tartan, a pattern of crossing coloured stripes.

clue.text: Attempt to ensnare red cardinal, say

indicators.note: to ensnare is to trap, so the first word traps the colour inside it

parts.note: a bid is an attempt
R is the usual abbreviation for red

explanation.surface: Trying to trap a scarlet cardinal, the songbird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red cardinal' sounds like a churchman in scarlet robes; the cardinal in the definition is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The cardinal is a red North American songbird, so it is an example of a bird.

clue.text: Frenchman has to see inside apartment

indicators.note: inside places the verb's word within the name of the man from France

parts.note: Pierre is a typical French man's name
to see someone is to date them

explanation.definitionFit: A pied-à-terre is a small second apartment kept in a city for occasional stays.

clue.text: Persevere flying kite that contains ribbon from the other side

indicators.note: coming from the other side means reading from the end back to the start
contains says the scrambled word holds the other piece inside itself
a flying kite twists and loops about the sky, so its letters move into a different order

parts.note: taken as written, then mixed
tape is a narrow ribbon of material

explanation.surface: Advice to a child struggling with a kite whose tail streamer is on the wrong side: don't give up.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep at it is the idiom for persisting with a task, which is persevering.

clue.text: Papa eats unfinished part of an egg that's not quite fresh

parts.note: the yolk is the yellow part of an egg
